paras: The killing of Warren Edwards and Henry Landers was the death of two Black men at the hands of a white officer in Atlanta, Georgia, reported in March 1919. According to a brief Black-press dispatch, the two had been playing cards and were killed when they tried to escape, and the dispatch called the deaths murder.

A dispatch datelined Atlanta, March 13, 1919, stated that Edwards and Landers, "two Negroes engaged in a little card game," were "brutally murdered by a white officer here when they attempted to escape." The dispatch did not name the officer, give the date or place of the killing within the city, or say whether the men had been arrested or on what charge. Its reference to an escape suggests an arrest connected with the card game, but that is not stated.
No report of an inquest, an arrest of the officer, or any official or community response appears in the coverage.

The story reached readers only as a single sentence circulated by the Associated Negro Press. The Baltimore Afro-American printed it on its front page on March 14 under the headline "WHITE OFFICER KILLS TWO," foregrounding the race of the killer. The next day the Omaha Monitor ran the identical text on page one as "OFFICER KILLS CARD PLAYER," a headline that put the card game beside the killing.

A week later the Dallas Express included the brief, without a headline, in a column of Associated Negro Press items from the South, all datelined March 20. In every version the Black press combined the officer's apparent justification, an attempted escape, with its own verdict that the men were "brutally murdered."

The dateline differs between printings, March 13 in the Baltimore and Omaha papers and March 20 in the Dallas Express, though the wording is the same. Because every item in the Dallas column carries March 20 and the brief had already appeared on March 14, the later date appears to be the column's date rather than the date of the killing.

accounts.label: Associated Negro Press brief
accounts.gist: Two Black men playing cards in Atlanta were 'brutally murdered by a white officer' when they attempted to escape; no name for the officer, no arrest charge, and no follow-up are given.

framing.detail: The Baltimore Afro-American headlined it 'WHITE OFFICER KILLS TWO' and the brief called the deaths 'brutally murdered', setting the 'little card game' against the officer's use of deadly force.
The Omaha Monitor ran the same brief on page one under 'OFFICER KILLS CARD PLAYER'.
The Dallas Express carried the brief without a headline inside an Associated Negro Press column of Southern items datelined March 20.

conflicts.note: The text is identical; every item in the Dallas Express column carries March 20, which looks like a column date, so the earlier March 13 dateline (also printed earlier, March 14) is the better guide. Neither is stated as the date of the killing.

Dateline only (March 13; March 20 in a later reprint); the killing date is not given.
